rationale: The candidate reads coherently in all four views as one compact, low-rise neighborhood mass rather than a collection of colliding fragments. The dominant gesture is legible: a swollen central body with a west-side public notch, yielding a usable ground threshold aligned to the required access side. In top and oblique views, the mass remains continuous and spatially consistent, with the opening clearly registered as a carved edge rather than a decorative cut. The silhouette is competent but somewhat generic and blocky; the stepped/angled roof-like variation helps, but the section still feels more like a mass with a notch than a fully articulated neighborhood living section. It is program-appropriate because it supports active ground relation, public void, and a calm upper mass without drifting into a tower or large-span hall typology. The main limitation is that the void is modest and the section does not yet strongly express inhabited terrace/public sequence, so the form is acceptable but not exceptional.
